articles.title: FlightAware drops lawsuit against Kalshi one day after filing
articles.summary: FlightAware voluntarily dismissed its suit against Kalshi over alleged unauthorized data/trademark use in flight-cancellation markets just one day after filing. Kalshi simultaneously changed its market language from "verified from FlightAware" to "verified from Primary Source Agency," suggesting the parties settled privately. Kalshi still faces active suits and injunctions in New York, Washington, and Michigan over sports-event contracts.

articles.title: CFTC Sues Goliath Ventures Over Alleged $397M DeFi Liquidity Pool Ponzi
articles.summary: The CFTC and SEC filed simultaneous civil suits against Goliath Ventures Inc. and CEO Christopher Delgado, alleging a $397 million Ponzi scheme from November 2022 through February 2026 in which approximately 1,600 customers were told their BTC and ETH would earn 36% annual yields in DEX liquidity pools. Goliath issued fabricated account statements while directing no capital to any DeFi protocol, funneling $174 million to staff as recruiting commissions, $87 million in Ponzi payments to existing customers, and $48 million to Delgado personally for luxury real estate, vehicles, and jewelry. Delgado pleaded guilty in June to wire fraud conspiracy and money laundering charges, and a bankruptcy receiver was appointed in March. The same-day CFTC-SEC filing demonstrates both agencies asserting parallel jurisdiction over crypto fraud, with CFTC Chairman Michael Selig citing an aggressive mandate to police crypto asset markets.

articles.title: Neutrl: Yield Without a Cycle
articles.summary: Crypto-native carry strategies face a structural timing mismatch: funding rates and basis spreads are royalties on speculative activity, so delta-neutral books earn worst when stablecoin demand peaks, a dynamic visible in H1 2026 when top-30 altcoin perpetual volume fell 30%, from $8.4B to $5.9B daily. Neutrl sidesteps this by buying private company locked shares at a 15% discount to the reference price and shorting the equity perpetual referencing the same name, hedging directional exposure from day one. Funding on the short leg averaged 10.9% annualized over a late-May to mid-July window, delivering roughly 20.5 points of total return over a six-month hold.

articles.title: Pudgy Penguins Co-Founder Launches NFT Mint on Robinhood Chain
articles.summary: Cole Villemain, removed from Pudgy Penguins in January 2022 amid treasury misuse allegations and scrutinized by ZachXBT, sold out a 44,444-piece NFT collection called Spritehood on Robinhood Chain in 57 minutes on August 11, generating $1.28M (684.28 ETH) across two tiers priced at $17 and $117. The Spritehood smart contract remains unverified on Robinhood Chain's Blockscout explorer, preventing buyers from auditing token mechanics and distribution terms. Villemain has promised future "infrastructure and mechanisms" without publishing verified contract code, and community observers have labeled the project a cash grab with unresolved questions about viability on the chain.

articles.title: $FIGR: The Market May Be Underwriting the Wrong Business
articles.summary: Figure has transitioned from balance-sheet lender to capital-light marketplace operator on Provenance blockchain rails: partner-originated loans reached 78% of Q1 2026 volume, Figure Connect grew from $8M to $1.6B in seven quarters, and ecosystem/technology fees expanded from 5% to 28% of revenue. The pending Kiavi acquisition adds $7B in annual residential transition loan origination at roughly 40% EBITDA margins, volume that should route through the same infrastructure without requiring additional capital deployment. Despite 91% incremental EBITDA margins in 2025 and adjusted EBITDA expanding from negative 4% to 49%, FIGR trades at roughly 12x EBITDA, in line with specialty lenders rather than the Tradeweb/ICE comps the business now resembles. Thin sell-side coverage and FIGR's legacy classification as a crypto proxy have left the market pricing the old balance-sheet model rather than the fee-generating marketplace.

articles.title: How to Turn $HYPE Funding Rates into Profit
articles.summary: Boros protocol lets traders isolate and trade funding rates as a standalone asset through Yield Units (YU), instruments that pay a fixed rate against the floating funding of a specific perpetual venue. A 4.03pp gap currently exists between HYPE's fixed rate on Hyperliquid (7.93%) and Bybit (3.89%), representing a spread that locks in at trade open and resolves over a 17-day window. The four-leg structure shorts YU on the Hyperliquid market and longs YU on Bybit, then offsets each leg with an opposing HYPE perpetual on the respective exchange, canceling both floating funding obligations and directional price exposure. The remaining return is the fixed rate differential, scaling to 40.30% APR at 10x leverage with no HYPE price risk.

articles.title: Who actually captures value in crypto
articles.summary: Analysis estimates on-chain protocol revenue at roughly $8 billion in 2025 versus roughly $70 billion (range $60-100B) for off-chain/centralized crypto companies (Coinbase, Tether, Binance, Robinhood's crypto arm, etc.), an 8.5x gap. Applying generous multiples, that implies on-chain's entire addressable market cap is about $168 billion versus roughly $840 billion for centralized players, meaning the whole centralized crypto industry is worth about as much as a single AI lab like OpenAI or Anthropic. On-chain revenue is dominated by L1/L2 chains (~49%). Off-chain is dominated by exchanges/brokers (~66%) and stablecoin issuers (~19%). Centralized players win by sitting closer to end users and abstracting away crypto's complexity.

articles.title: Tokenized Stocks: The Next Battleground
articles.summary: Tokenized equities reached ~$1.9B in market size, a 6.5x increase since January 2025, while the tokenized Treasury market stagnated at $15B after April 2026. The SEC's January 2026 taxonomy established four structural models. The Linked Security structure (DeFi-composable, no voting rights, unavailable to US investors) has captured the most share, with Ondo at 45.9% ($851M across 406 equities) and xStocks at 26% ($482M across 183 equities), both operating via Jersey-regulated SPVs. Traditional market infrastructure accelerated entry in mid-2026: DTCC began limited QQQ/SPY tokenization on July 15 after an SEC no-action letter, Nasdaq secured rule-change approval in March 2026 and is building a permissionless gateway with Kraken parent Payward, and NYSE filed its own rule change while signing an MOU with Securitize. Coinbase announced a 1:1 stock-backed token product for non-US customers with onchain usability but has not yet launched.

articles.title: Estimating Circle's Q2 earnings from on-chain data alone
articles.summary: Allium Research used adjusted USDC circulating supply, Coinbase wallet labels, and published rate schedules to estimate Circle's Q2 reserve income before earnings, landing at $667.4 million against Circle's reported $667.7 million.
